memories.statement: Invoice.InvoiceDate spans 2009-01-01 to 2013-12-22 (412 invoices, 2,328.60), so "this year"/"last year" mean 2013/2012, not the current date; 2013 is partial (80 invoices vs 83 in each earlier year).
memories.evidence: SELECT strftime('%Y',InvoiceDate) y, COUNT(*), ROUND(SUM(Total),2) FROM Invoice GROUP BY y
memories.review_note: Evidence checks out, but the "this year = 2013" part duplicates owner decision M010 (accepted), and the statement packs several claims. Resubmit as one sentence, e.g. "Invoice data runs 2009-01-01 to 2013-12-22; 2013 is partial (80 invoices vs 83 in each earlier year)", topic dates.

memories.statement: Sales include video: 111 InvoiceLines (220.89 of 2,328.60, about 9.5%) are MediaType "Protected MPEG-4 video file" (TV shows, movies), so "music revenue" is ambiguous; filter via Track.MediaTypeId.
memories.evidence: SELECT m.Name, COUNT(*), ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice*il.Quantity),2) FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t USING(TrackId) JOIN MediaType m USING(MediaTypeId) GROUP BY m.Name

memories.statement: Genre mixes in video categories (TV Shows, Drama, Comedy, Sci Fi & Fantasy, Science Fiction), so genre rankings of revenue include non-music; e.g. TV Shows is the 5th top-selling "genre" at 93.53.
memories.evidence: SELECT g.Name, COUNT(*) FROM Track t JOIN Genre g USING(GenreId) WHERE t.MediaTypeId=3 GROUP BY 1

memories.statement: Playlist names repeat (Music, Movies, TV Shows, Audiobooks twice each, with identical contents for Music ids 1 and 8), and PlaylistTrack has 8,715 rows for 3,503 distinct tracks, so join by PlaylistId and use COUNT(DISTINCT TrackId).
memories.evidence: SELECT Name, COUNT(*) FROM Playlist GROUP BY Name HAVING COUNT(*)>1
memories.review_note: Verified: 4 duplicated names, Music 1 and 8 identical, 8,715 rows / 3,503 tracks.

memories.statement: Sales by employee can only go via Customer.SupportRepId (Invoice has no employee); only the 3 Sales Support Agents (ids 3,4,5; 21/20/18 customers) have customers, the other 5 employees have none.
memories.evidence: SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.Title, COUNT(c.CustomerId) FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId=e.EmployeeId GROUP BY 1

memories.statement: Revenue is Invoice.Total, which equals SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice*Quantity) (2,328.60 both ways); every Quantity is 1, so line counts equal units sold; don't sum Total after joining to InvoiceLine (it multiplies).
memories.evidence: SELECT (SELECT SUM(Total) FROM Invoice), (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice*Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), (SELECT MAX(Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine)

memories.statement: Track.UnitPrice is 0.99 except 213 video tracks at 1.99; 1,519 of 3,503 tracks were never sold, so inner joins from Track to InvoiceLine drop them; use LEFT JOIN for catalog-wide counts.
memories.evidence: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM InvoiceLine)

memories.statement: Invoice.BillingCountry always equals the customer's Country (0 mismatches), and Customer.State is NULL for 29 of 59 customers, so country analysis is safe either way but state analysis is incomplete.
memories.evidence: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c USING(CustomerId) WHERE i.BillingCountry<>c.Country

memories.statement: Music revenue and music sales exclude video tracks (MediaType 'Protected MPEG-4 video file'); report video sales separately only when asked.
Treat 2013, the latest year in the data, as the current year: 'this year' means 2013 and 'last year' means 2012.
Rank 'top' or 'best' customers by total spend (sum of Invoice.Total), not by number of purchases.
When a ranking has a tie, always show all the tied names instead of cutting the list off at the limit.
memories.source: User said: "whenever there's a tie in a ranking, always show all the tied names instead of cutting the list off."
memories.review_note: User-stated rule, reusable, no duplicate or conflict. New topic 'rankings' is justified since the rule applies beyond customers.
